taskDescription: Arrange the layers of the epidermis in order from deepest to most superficial.
paragraphs: Stratum basale — dividing stem cells, with melanocytes and Merkel cells
Stratum spinosum — cells linked by desmosomes; Langerhans cells present
Stratum granulosum — cells with keratohyalin granules, beginning to die
Stratum lucidum — a clear layer found only in thick skin
Stratum corneum — dead, keratin-filled cells forming the waterproof barrier

overallFeedback.feedback: The five layers from deep to superficial are basale, spinosum, granulosum, lucidum and corneum. New keratinocytes arise in the basale, are pushed upward as they keratinise and die, and are shed from the corneum — this orderly turnover is the basis of wound healing from the intact basal layer.
